recommendation_1: Reduce mid_dim from 100 to 32 to significantly decrease the number of trainable parameters and memory footprint.
rationale_1: Lowering mid_dim reduces the hidden layer size, directly decreasing both RAM usage and computational requirements, which aligns with Green AI principles and maintains compatibility with Flower's federated learning framework.
recommendation_3: Apply L1 Unstructured Pruning to remove redundant weights post-training using torch.nn.utils.prune and ensure prune.remove is called to maintain a clean state_dict for Flower compatibility.
rationale_3: Pruning removes unnecessary connections, reducing model size and computational overhead without compromising performance, enabling efficient deployment in federated environments.
recommendation_4: Switch to Bfloat16 Autocast for CPU-based training/inference to reduce memory usage and improve numerical stability.
rationale_4: Using bf16 reduces memory consumption compared to FP32 and provides sufficient precision for training, especially beneficial when operating under strict RAM constraints in Flower-based systems.
recommendation_5: Replace ReLU activation with LeakyReLU (negative_slope=0.01) to improve gradient flow and reduce dead neuron issues, leading to better training efficiency.
rationale_5: LeakyReLU prevents vanishing gradients more effectively than standard ReLU, improving convergence speed and reducing training time, thus lowering energy expenditure per epoch.
recommendation_6: Remove the explicit log_softmax call in the forward pass and rely on CrossEntropyLoss to handle it internally to reduce redundant computations.
rationale_6: This avoids double computation of log-softmax and simplifies the forward pass, contributing to reduced memory pressure and improved runtime efficiency within Flower’s distributed training loop.
